messages:
alan (Customer): Hey team — hitting a weird streaming issue. Using SSE for streaming chat responses, but the client sometimes gets a perfectly valid JSON stream and the last JSON object is cut off. No `finish_reason` and client-side parser errors on the final chunk. Repro steps attached below.

maya (Support): Sorry you're seeing this, alan. Can you paste the minimal curl or client code you used to reproduce and the request id from the response headers if available? Also which region + model?

alan (Customer): repro: `curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-...\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=rlm-large\"` — response looks fine until the last chunk which is like: 

```
data: {"id":"tok_abc","text":"...","role":"assistant"}
data: {"id":"tok_def","text":"final part...
```

And then connection closes immediately. The client tries to parse and fails with "unexpected end of JSON input". No `finish_reason` field in the last object. Request headers returned `x-request-id: rq_20240308_17` and `x-region: us-west-2`.

maya (Support): Thanks — that x-request-id helps. @ajay can you triage ingress/proxy timeouts for rq_20240308_17 in us-west-2?

ajay (SRE): On it. Quick questions: 1) Is the client behind a proxy/load balancer? 2) Any intermittent 502/504s or just silent disconnect with TCP FIN? Also can you check if the client receives a `Content-Length`? SSE streams should be chunked (no Content-Length).

alan (Customer): Client is a web app using EventSource in Chrome, no custom proxy. I captured network (HAR). It's a clean 200 then stream bytes then a FIN. No 502/504. No `Content-Length`.

ajay (SRE): Thanks. I pulled the platform logs for rq_20240308_17 — I see the serving runtime closed the connection at 2024-03-08T17:12:04.123Z with a write error to the socket: `write: broken pipe`. Prior to that there was a sequence of SSE data frames. No internal 5xx from model runner.

jonathan (Eng): Could be client-side read buffer reaching EOF if there's an intermediate reverse proxy with an idle timeout. Our NGINX ingress sometimes closes connections on long-lived streams if keepalive or proxy_read_timeout not set high enough. Which host did the client connect to (edge hostname)?

alan (Customer): edge hostname: api-us-west2.redwood.ai. Client is on mobile network, might be flaky.

maya (Support): Possible hypothesis: mobile carrier drop -> socket closed -> server tries to write remaining bytes -> gets EPIPE -> runtime aborts and doesn't emit final sentinel object (so `finish_reason` missing). Workaround: we can make runtime emit final state in a persisted event before the final write completes, but need eng to confirm.

ajay (SRE): Reproducer idea: if you intentionally cut the TCP (simulated with `tc qdisc` or by toggling mobile wifi), you'll see identical behavior. I also noticed our connection drains if kernel send buffer is full. Two action items: 1) collect a pcap (tcpdump) at edge for the session. 2) Eng to add a safety flush: write a small final `data: {"finish_reason":"server_disconnect"}

jonathan (Eng): Agreed. We should also avoid leaving parseable JSON half-written. Proposed change: runtime should send a final small SSE event before closing that is single-line and newline-delimited, e.g.: `data: {"type":"terminal","finish_reason":null}` — but better to include a non-null finish_reason like `connection_lost`. Also we can add a `:heartbeat` comment every 15s to keep intermediates alive.

alan (Customer): Could you share a short-term client workaround? We can patch the app quickly.

maya (Support): Short term: 1) When parsing SSE, tolerate truncated final chunk by buffering until stream close and treat parser EOF as soft-finish if last successfully parsed JSON exists. 2) Implement client-side reconnect with resume semantics: store last token id and on reconnect send `?last_event_id=<id>`; our platform supports dedup if we receive resume but note current resume flow may replay partially emitted tokens.

ajay (SRE): Also set EventSource polyfill with `withCredentials = false` and enable `keepalive` (where supported). If you use fetch+readable-stream, you can attempt to read until stream close and then fallback to re-request with `?resume=true`.

deploy-bot: Created ticket INF-5583 for runtime final-event sentinel and INF-5584 for adding more aggressive edge keepalive. Linked: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-5583

maya (Support): Next steps for us: alan, can you upload the HAR/pcap and your client console logs to the ticket? We will triage with eng and SRE. For now, treat the final-JSON-parse error as transient; we may mark it as "best-effort graceful degradation" until runtime change is live.

alan (Customer): Uploaded HAR and console logs to INF-5583. Thanks — will implement client tolerate/ reconnect patch and report back.

ajay (SRE): FYI — I added proxy read timeout increases for a small subset of workers in us-west-2 to test, and enabled heartbeat comments on the edge for 1% of traffic. We'll monitor errorrate for the request id series.

jonathan (Eng): Patch queued: runtime will now emit a one-line terminal event on connection error: `data: {"terminal":true,"finish_reason":"connection_lost"}`. We'll roll canary next week.

maya (Support): Closing loop when canary is live. Marking this thread resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
